about: Every ready-to-paste prompt on the site, plus the Prompt Optimizer templates. To compose an assignment yourself: start with optimizer.sections, fill each {{field}} from the chosen type's defaults (overridden by the user's answers), apply |list and |numbered filters, drop sections whose 'needs' fields are empty, and render titles as '## Title' (markdown) or <tag>...</tag> (xml).

repository_prompts.starter:
Use https://github.com/Open-Medical-Affairs/Medical-Affairs-Skills
Read AGENTS.md and start a workshop mission using the bundled synthetic data.
Begin with oncology field insights unless I choose another area.
Find the three things leadership should know, explain why they matter,
and create a concise leadership brief with source records and next actions.
Use available public APIs only when useful, keeping real evidence separate
from fictional workshop facts. Do not ask me to connect company systems.
If you cannot retrieve the repository, tell me which starter file to upload.
repository_prompts.quickstart:
Use https://github.com/Open-Medical-Affairs/Medical-Affairs-Skills
Read AGENTS.md. Start the field-insights workshop mission using the oncology
synthetic data. Find the three things leadership should know, explain why,
and create a short brief with sources and next actions.
Do not ask me to connect company systems. Use public scientific sources only
when useful and keep them separate from fictional workshop data.
repository_prompts.capstone:
Using this repository and the synthetic data for our therapeutic area, prepare
the next 30 days of Medical Affairs work. Choose the important priorities,
create a leadership brief, action tracker and scientific briefing, and keep
track of which sources each output depends on. Use the thirty-day-capstone
mission. Complete the supported work and identify the decisions still needed.
repository_prompts.change_card:
This new information has arrived. Identify which conclusions and files it
affects. Update the relevant work, preserve the old version, and show me the
changes with their reasons. Tell me what still cannot be determined.
repository_prompts.msl_pre_call:
Use the Medical Affairs Skills repository to prepare my next HCP engagement.
In workshop mode use oncology HCP-138. Gather the prior interactions, open
tasks and access context, create a one-page pre-call brief, and propose three
neutral scientific questions. Prepare the administrative records as drafts.
Do not invent a meeting date, HCP statement or completed follow-up.
next_moves: Show me what supports the most important conclusion.
Make this a two-page brief for an MSL.
Now prepare an advisory board around the unanswered questions.
recovery: Use the supplied synthetic sources. Continue without live APIs.
Give the complete brief here if you cannot create the file.
Show what is already saved and the next unfinished step.
Which source supports that number? Keep it unresolved if none does.

types.label: KOL pre-call brief
types.role: a senior Medical Science Liaison preparing a scientific exchange
steps: Gather prior interactions, open commitments and what has changed since the last meeting.
Identify what this expert genuinely cares about and where our evidence is weak.
Draft neutral scientific questions to ask, and the hard questions they will likely ask us, with the evidence to have ready.

defaults.goal: Walk into a 30-minute scientific exchange with the first expert in the KOL dossiers fully prepared, including an honest answer to their strongest objection.
defaults.audience: Me, the MSL, in the ten minutes before the meeting.
defaults.constraints:
Two pages maximum: it gets read in ten minutes.
No promotional language: this is scientific exchange.
defaults.deliverable:
Two-page meeting brief (Word + PDF)
Questions to ask, likely questions, evidence and unresolved gaps
defaults.checks:
Every claim about the expert traces to a dossier or interaction note
Unresolved evidence is stated plainly, not smoothed over
No meeting facts are invented
defaults.human_stop:
Contacting the expert or scheduling anything
Anything that looks like an off-label request

types.label: Field insights synthesis
types.role: a Medical Affairs insights lead reporting to leadership
steps: Deduplicate contacts and separate observations from insights.
Find the three most consequential insights: what is happening, why it matters, what it changes.
Capture disagreements, weak signals and what the field did not say.
Recommend one concrete next action per insight with an accountable role.

defaults.goal: Leadership knows the three field insights that should change what we do this quarter, each with an owner and a next action.
defaults.audience: Medical Affairs leadership, four minutes to read.
defaults.constraints:
Themes with counts are not insights: explain why it matters and what it changes.
State confidence for each insight and why.
defaults.deliverable:
Leadership brief (Word + PDF)
Insight table with source record IDs
Simulated safety escalation and missing-information list
defaults.checks:
Every insight cites source record IDs
Safety findings appear before the analysis
Each action names an accountable role
defaults.human_stop:
Routing any safety finding
Sharing the brief beyond our team

types.label: Congress readout
types.role: a congress intelligence lead in Medical Affairs
steps: State what we expected before the congress.
Compare what was presented with those expectations and with the current medical plan.
Apply the same scepticism to our own data as to competitors'.
Recommend what changes in the plan, what does not, and why.

defaults.goal: Leadership knows in four minutes what changed at the congress and what we should do about it.
defaults.audience: Medical leadership and brand medical leads.
defaults.constraints:
One page, four sections: what changed, why it matters, what to watch, what we should do.
A summary of presentations is not intelligence.
defaults.deliverable:
One-page congress readout (Word + PDF)
Change recommendations with evidence limitations
defaults.checks:
Every 'what changed' item is compared against a stated prior expectation
Evidence limitations stay attached to each finding
Anything contradicting a current claim is flagged
defaults.human_stop: Changing an approved medical plan or claim

types.label: Medical information response
steps: Triage the enquiries by urgency and type.
Surface potential safety issues before drafting.
Draft responses supported only by the supplied sources.
Log every gap where the evidence does not answer the question.

defaults.goal: The enquiry queue is triaged, every answerable enquiry has a draft response, and every gap is logged.
defaults.audience: The medical information team and the reviewing medical signatory.
defaults.constraints:
Do not infer approval in other countries.
Answer the question asked; do not volunteer off-label information.
defaults.deliverable:
Triage register
Draft responses and gap log
Simulated safety routing list
defaults.checks:
Every response cites the supporting source
No response is marked as sent
Safety items are routed before drafting
defaults.human_stop:
Sending any response
Any real (non-simulated) safety case

types.label: Evidence gap map
steps: List the gaps and, for each, the decision it blocks and whose decision it is.
Separate evidence gaps from communication gaps.
Propose the study design that would close each gap that matters, with cost.
Allocate the budget with an explicit funding line and what is lost below it.

defaults.goal: A ranked evidence gap map with a funded portfolio inside the budget ceiling and an explicit line below which we decline.
defaults.constraints:
Do not propose a study just because data are missing: explain the decision it changes.
Check what we could answer from data we already hold.
defaults.deliverable:
Ranked gap map (spreadsheet or table)
Committee brief with trade-offs
defaults.checks:
Every gap names the decision it blocks
The allocation adds up to the ceiling or less
Duplicated and dependent projects are reconciled
defaults.human_stop: Committing budget or approving a study

types.label: Advisory board package
types.role: a medical strategy lead designing an advisory board
steps: Identify the unanswered questions that justify seeking external advice.
Drop any question the evidence does not justify, and say why.
Write the charter, discussion guide and advisor briefs.
Build the pre-read deck.

defaults.goal: An advisory board worth holding: five unanswered questions, each tied to a decision, with the full briefing package ready for review.
defaults.audience: Internal approvers first, then the external advisors.
defaults.constraints:
Questions seek advice, not endorsement.
Apparent consensus in past transcripts is challenged, not assumed.
defaults.deliverable:
Board charter and discussion guide
Pre-read deck (PowerPoint + PDF)
Advisor briefs
defaults.checks:
Each question links to a decision and an evidence gap
No question is leading or promotional
All figures trace to sources

types.label: Publication plan
steps: Work backwards from what each audience is trying to decide.
Show where we over-communicate and where we are silent.
Separate evidence gaps (research) from communication gaps (publish).
Sequence the next 12 months of outputs.

defaults.goal: A 12-month scientific communication strategy we can defend, including what to stop publishing.
defaults.constraints:
A strategy, not a list of papers sequenced by data availability.
Negative and neutral results are planned for, not hidden.
defaults.deliverable:
Strategy brief (Word + PDF)
Publication roadmap table
defaults.checks:
Each planned output names its audience and the decision it informs
Evidence gaps and communication gaps are labelled separately
Reported numbers match the source tables
defaults.human_stop: Submitting or committing to a journal or congress

types.label: Launch readiness & launch plan
steps: Assess every launch dependency against the readiness register.
Never average a critical red dependency into a green score.
Build the remediation plan with owners and dates.
Draft the medical launch plan for the first 90 days.

defaults.goal: A clear launch gate verdict, a remediation plan for every red or amber item, and a first-90-days medical launch plan.
defaults.audience: The launch team and medical leadership.
defaults.constraints:
A red safety or regulatory dependency blocks green, whatever the average.
Every action has an owner and a date.
defaults.deliverable:
Gate assessment
Remediation tracker
Leadership brief and 90-day medical launch plan
defaults.checks:
Every red item has a remediation owner
The verdict follows the worst critical dependency
Open MLR comments are reflected
defaults.human_stop:
Declaring launch readiness
Anything that needs MLR approval

types.label: Plain-language summary
types.role: a plain-language writer working with patient partners
steps: Pull the key findings from the source.
Rewrite for a lay reader, keeping every limitation and safety finding.
Check readability and remove jargon.
Check every number against the source.

defaults.goal: A plain-language summary a patient or caregiver can understand that stays faithful to the study.
defaults.audience: Patients and caregivers with no medical training.
defaults.constraints:
No promotional language and no claims beyond the study.
Keep harms as visible as benefits.
defaults.deliverable:
Plain-language summary (Word + PDF)
Number-check log against the source
defaults.checks:
Every number matches the source
Limitations and safety results are included
Reading level suits a general audience

types.label: Agent swarm / coordinator
types.role: the coordinator of a team of Medical Affairs agents
steps: Break the goal into workstreams and assign each to a specialist sub-agent (or run them in sequence if you cannot spawn agents).
Give each workstream its own inputs, deliverable and proof of done.
Track which sources each output depends on.
Merge the work, resolve conflicts between workstreams and keep a change log.

defaults.goal: A coordinated 30-day Medical Affairs plan: leadership brief, action tracker and scientific briefing, with source dependencies so new evidence can update the affected work.
defaults.audience: Medical Affairs leadership and the workstream owners.
defaults.context: medical-plan.md, product-profile.md, field-observations.csv, evidence-landscape.md, integrated-evidence-plan.csv, launch-readiness-register.md
defaults.constraints:
Each sub-agent gets only the inputs it needs.
When new information arrives, update only the affected work and preserve the old version.
defaults.deliverable:
Workstream assignment table (agent, inputs, deliverable, proof)
Leadership brief, 30-day action tracker, scientific briefing
Source dependency map and change log
defaults.checks:
Every output lists its source dependencies
Conflicts between workstreams are resolved or escalated
The tracker has an owner and date per action
defaults.human_stop:
Any trade-off between workstreams that changes priorities
Anything outside the agreed budget

# Assignment: Publication plan
You are a scientific communications lead. This is an assignment, not a question: do the work end to end and hand back finished deliverables, not advice.

## Goal: what done looks like
Decide what we should publish over the next 12 months, what we should stop, and make every scientific output consistent with the source data.

## Who it is for
The publications steering committee.

## Context to use
- Use https://github.com/Open-Medical-Affairs/Medical-Affairs-Skills. Read AGENTS.md first, then load these skills and their requirements: scientific-communication-strategy, scientific-manuscript, plain-language-summary.
- Workshop mode: use the oncology synthetic data in Data-Sources/synthetic/oncology-mm/ (mission `publication` in workshop/catalog.json). Read files there by name.
- publication-plan.md, evidence-landscape.md, field-observations.csv, medical-plan.md, product-profile.md

## How to work
1. Inventory the inputs. List what is missing before you start, then continue with what you have.
2. Scan human-sourced records for possible safety findings first.
3. Work backwards from what each audience is trying to decide.
4. Show where we over-communicate and where we are silent.
5. Separate evidence gaps (research) from communication gaps (publish).
6. Sequence the next 12 months of outputs.
7. Challenge your own draft with deliverable-quality-review and fix what it finds.
8. Deliver designed files where your environment allows; otherwise give the complete content in your reply and say so.

## House rules and boundaries
- A strategy, not a list of papers sequenced by data availability.
- Negative and neutral results are planned for, not hidden.
- Do not send, post, publish or change any external system. Prepare drafts only.
- Never invent a citation, number or quote. If no source supports a claim, say so and leave it unresolved.
- Before any analysis, surface possible safety findings (adverse events, product complaints) with the verbatim and flag them for routing.
- Keep any fictional practice data and real evidence clearly separate. Mark every output DRAFT.

## Deliverable
- Strategy brief (Word + PDF)
- Publication roadmap table

## Proof of done (verify before you hand over)
- Each planned output names its audience and the decision it informs
- Evidence gaps and communication gaps are labelled separately
- Reported numbers match the source tables

## Stop and come back to me before you
- Submitting or committing to a journal or congress

## When you finish
Tell me what you did, what you could not do, and which decisions are still mine. I am the final judge of this work.

## Goal: what done looks like
A coordinated 30-day Medical Affairs plan: leadership brief, action tracker and scientific briefing, with source dependencies so new evidence can update the affected work.

## Who it is for
Medical Affairs leadership and the workstream owners.

## Context to use
- Use https://github.com/Open-Medical-Affairs/Medical-Affairs-Skills. Read AGENTS.md first, then load these skills and their requirements: medical-affairs-orchestrator, medical-strategy-plan, field-insight-synthesis, integrated-evidence-plan, executive-briefing.

- medical-plan.md, product-profile.md, field-observations.csv, evidence-landscape.md, integrated-evidence-plan.csv, launch-readiness-register.md

## How to work
1. Inventory the inputs. List what is missing before you start, then continue with what you have.
2. Scan human-sourced records for possible safety findings first.
3. Break the goal into workstreams and assign each to a specialist sub-agent (or run them in sequence if you cannot spawn agents).
4. Give each workstream its own inputs, deliverable and proof of done.
5. Track which sources each output depends on.
6. Merge the work, resolve conflicts between workstreams and keep a change log.

- When new information arrives, update only the affected work and preserve the old version.
- Do not send, post, publish or change any external system. Prepare drafts only.
- Never invent a citation, number or quote. If no source supports a claim, say so and leave it unresolved.
- Before any analysis, surface possible safety findings (adverse events, product complaints) with the verbatim and flag them for routing.
- Keep any fictional practice data and real evidence clearly separate. Mark every output DRAFT.

## Deliverable
- Workstream assignment table (agent, inputs, deliverable, proof)
- Leadership brief, 30-day action tracker, scientific briefing
- Source dependency map and change log

## Proof of done (verify before you hand over)
- Every output lists its source dependencies
- Conflicts between workstreams are resolved or escalated
- The tracker has an owner and date per action

## Stop and come back to me before you
- Any trade-off between workstreams that changes priorities
- Anything outside the agreed budget

## When you finish
Tell me what you did, what you could not do, and which decisions are still mine. I am the final judge of this work.
